subs.en: Good afternoon, Tiji and Arzak.
No, today I'm here as a property agent.
Back then I sold my voice. Now I sell homes.
Masya Allah!
I never expected it. 13 years ago I changed careers.
As a property agent I get to help so many people solve problems and reach their property dreams.
So the fulfilment is different.
On radio, our happiness came from making listeners happy.
As an agent, it comes from helping my clients reach their life goals.

name: Nona Kirana
cta_small: Kira your numbers dulu. WhatsApp Nona 8268 1111 atau DM sahaja.
title: Upgrade tak semestinya private

subs.en: Why do people upgrade? What is it?
When we talk about upgrading, it doesn't have to mean moving to private property.
Some people start with a 3-room BTO.
Then once the kids come, they need more space and comfort for the family, and they come to see me.
"Nona, on my salary, single income, wife at home, can I get enough loan to upgrade to a 5-room?"
That's where I do a detailed calculation,
look at their budget, because we don't want them to overstretch or pay more than they can afford.

title: Perumahan dan persaraan berkait rapat
kicker: 13 tahun bantu orang jual beli rumah

subs.en: In my opinion, after 13 years helping people buy and sell,
housing and retirement are closely linked.
The decisions we make in our 30s and 40s decide what our retirement looks like.
Some people have the courage but not the means.
They want to buy a condo but actually can't afford it.
So it's hard. What can Nona do?
Usually I look at it from the budget.
Say they can only afford an Executive Maisonette.
Then no need to go all the way to private.
Because an Executive Maisonette is a type of housing I think is great. It has stairs.
Privacy like a landed home.

name: Nona Kirana
cta_small: Kira your numbers dulu. WhatsApp Nona 8268 1111 atau DM sahaja.
title: Strategi: private dulu, patah balik HDB

subs.en: I do recommend they move to private property,
because from experience, those who go private and later downsize back to HDB
end up with more cash left over,
so we top up the retirement account too.
Then at 65, CPF LIFE starts.
All of this I help with. We look at your numbers first,
before deciding which upgrade suits you and your family.
Before making this decision, do the sums and discuss first.
Listen to a qualified, licensed agent.

name: Nona Kirana
cta_small: Kira your numbers dulu. WhatsApp Nona 8268 1111 atau DM sahaja.
title: Go for the biggest HDB

popups.sub: the last EMs are ~36 years old

subs.en: Like I said, if you can afford it, I always say go for the biggest HDB.
Meaning, if you can buy the biggest, buy a jumbo, an Executive Maisonette, an Executive Apartment. Why?
The government no longer builds these.
The last Executive Maisonettes I know of are at Rivervale Crescent, about 36 years old now.
Since then they haven't built any.
So if you buy one, people say you're buying a rare item.
Because when we're old, the young ones will say: "Eh auntie, your house has stairs! So unique."
And they'll pay for a home that's no longer in production.
If you want one, the government isn't building more.
So for those who can afford it, I'd say buy the biggest.

name: Nona Kirana

title: Kisah pakcik Tampines: $300k cash & CPF LIFE penuh

subs.en: I have a case. This uncle,
when he was newly married, bought a 3-room in Tampines.
When he had three daughters, he moved to an Executive Apartment, also in Tampines.
When he reached his 60s, 68 if I'm not mistaken,
he said: it's just auntie and me now. The kids have all moved out.
This Executive Apartment is too big.
So what did he want?
A 3-room near Tampines Interchange, near the polyclinic.
Because when you're older, collecting medicine nearby is easier.
So what did Nona do? I sold the Executive Apartment.
We moved to a 3-room right next to Tampines Polyclinic.
And in the bank he had over $300,000 cash.
His Retirement Account was full too.
Meaning every month he gets the full CPF LIFE payout.

name: Nona Kirana

title: Bayar habis sebelum 55

popups.sub: the other half comes from cash

subs.en: For those of you who may have the means, in your 30s and 40s,
and feel you can stretch a little,
you must have a plan to pay it off before 55.
Why?
At 55 our Retirement Account kicks in.
Some don't meet the Full Retirement Sum, so all sorts of problems.
And our CPF contribution also drops.
If you used to have $1,000 to pay the home loan,
later it drops by 50% to only $500.
So $500 has to come out in cash.
That's when you hear people say: eh, I have to top up cash for my house.
That's what we want to avoid.

title: Bukan ejen jual, beli, bye-bye

subs.en: All of this, Nona will help with,
because usually a property agent does the sale and then it's bye-bye.
Bye, see you around. Usually that's the job.
But for me, I have a responsibility to help them plan.
Especially if they're in their 30s or 40s: yes, take the 25-year loan.
Then what?
The plan is: by 55, the house is fully paid.

name: Nona Kirana

title: Kakak 55, Abang 60, dan magic trick CPF

popups.sub: use retirement savings to clear the loan

subs.en: I once visited a home where the wife was fussing with her husband.
She's 55, he's 60.
Why was she fussing?
"We actually want to downgrade,
but look at these kids, all waiting for BTO, just back from studies, nobody wants to move out.
How can we downgrade?"
They live in an Executive Maisonette: four bedrooms, comfortable.
But the loan is still there.
"How do we pay? My husband no longer works."
Logically they should downgrade: move to a 3-room, pay it off.
But their life situation doesn't allow them to downgrade,
because the kids won't leave, and you love your kids.
That's why: imagine if they'd bought early and planned to pay it off,
they wouldn't need to sell under pressure.
But Nona had a magic trick.
What I told them then: do property pledging.
Property pledging: take money from your retirement savings to pay off the loan.
This is one option we can take,
but it's a CPF policy.
You need to know whether or not you qualify for property pledging.
